summary: When scribes and Pharisees demand a sign, Jesus offers only the sign of Jonah, points to One greater than Jonah and Solomon, and warns against inner darkness.
key_insight: The men of Nineveh repented with no miracle at all, only Jonah’s preaching, and the queen of Sheba traveled a great distance to hear Solomon. Jesus’ hearers had far more standing in front of them, “a greater than Jonah,” and still asked for proof.
story: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees spoke up: “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.” {Mt} The crowds were pressing in thick around Him. {Lk}

Jesus answered, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” As Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man would be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. {Mt} As Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man would be a sign to this generation. {Lk}

At the judgment, He said, the men of Nineveh will rise up and condemn this generation, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah, “and indeed a greater than Jonah is here.” The queen of the South will condemn it too, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, “and indeed a greater than Solomon is here.”

Then Jesus told what happens when an unclean spirit leaves a man. It wanders through dry places seeking rest and finds none. So it says, “I will return to my house from which I came.” It finds the house empty, {Mt} swept and put in order, and it brings back seven other spirits more wicked than itself. “The last state of that man is worse than the first. So shall it also be with this wicked generation.” {Mt}

As He was saying these things, a woman in the crowd called out, “Blessed is the womb that bore You, and the breasts which nursed You!” Jesus answered, “More than that, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it!” {Lk}

Luke records that Jesus followed His answer about Jonah with a word about light. No one lights a lamp and hides it in a secret place or under a basket; it goes on a lampstand, “that those who come in may see the light.” “The lamp of the body is the eye.” When the eye is good, the whole body is full of light; when it is bad, the body is full of darkness. “Therefore take heed that the light which is in you is not darkness.” {Lk}
differences: Matthew says the scribes and Pharisees asked for a sign. Luke ties the demand to the Beelzebub scene, where “others, testing Him, sought from Him a sign from heaven.”
Only Matthew explains the sign by Jonah’s “three days and three nights” in the fish. Luke says Jonah “became a sign to the Ninevites.”

The order varies. Matthew gives the sign before the returning spirit and names Nineveh before the queen of the South; Luke reverses both. Only Matthew says the house was “empty” and applies the picture to “this wicked generation.”
Only Luke records the woman who called out a blessing on Jesus’ mother.
Only Luke adds the sayings about the lamp and the eye (11:33–36). Matthew records similar words in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:15; 6:22–23).

fit.question: Luke places this teaching on Jesus’ later journey (Luke 11), in a different order, with the two examples reversed. Is this the same occasion as in Matthew?

points.label: Jesus repeated Himself
points.text: Jesus gave the sign of Jonah at least twice. Matthew records it here and again when Pharisees and Sadducees demand a sign near Magdala (Matthew 16:4). Luke’s sayings about the lamp and the eye, which Matthew gives in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:15; 6:22–23), show the same habit. A teacher who traveled for about three years naturally gave the same answer to the same demand in different places.

points.label: Arranged to make a point
points.text: If Matthew and Luke describe the same day, each has ordered the sayings for his purpose. Matthew moves straight from the demand to the answer. Luke keeps the warning about the returning spirit next to the Beelzebub debate it grows out of.

fit.note: Repeated teaching and sayings arranged by theme are both normal in honest reporting; neither changes what Jesus said.
fit.short: Jesus gave the sign of Jonah more than once (Matthew 16:4), and each writer arranges the sayings to make his point.

fit.question: Jesus said He would be “three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.” But He died on Friday afternoon and rose early on Sunday. How do these fit?

points.label: Counting by parts
points.text: Jews counted any part of a day as a whole day. Esther called for a fast of “three days, night or day,” then went to the king “on the third day” (Esther 4:16; 5:1). A later rabbinic saying states the rule: part of a day counts as the whole.

points.label: Jesus’ own phrases
points.text: Jesus also said He would be raised “the third day” (Matthew 16:21) and “after three days” (Mark 8:31). For Him and His hearers these described the same span of time.

points.label: Other proposals
points.text: A few place the crucifixion on Wednesday or Thursday to allow three full nights, taking the Sabbath that followed as a special feast-day Sabbath. Most read the Gospels’ own details as pointing to Friday: Jesus died on the Preparation Day, “the day before the Sabbath” (Mark 15:42), and the women “rested on the Sabbath according to the commandment” (Luke 23:56) before coming to the tomb on the first day of the week.

fit.note: The phrase is a Jewish way of counting days, not a stopwatch, and it fits the Gospels’ own timeline.
fit.short: Jews counted part of a day as a whole day. Jesus also said “the third day” and “after three days” for the same span.

scene.label: Jonah and Nineveh
scene.text: Nineveh was the capital of Assyria, Israel’s cruel enemy. Jonah preached there with no recorded miracle, and the people of Nineveh believed God, fasted and put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:5).

scene.label: The queen of the South
scene.text: Jesus means the queen of Sheba, from a kingdom far to the south, probably in southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions (1 Kings 10:1). To Jesus’ hearers, her homeland was the ends of the earth.

scene.label: “Adulterous generation”
scene.text: The prophets called Israel’s unfaithfulness to God adultery (Hosea 2; Jeremiah 3). Jesus uses the same charge: a generation that demands proof while ignoring God’s messenger is unfaithful to God Himself.

scene.label: A sign on demand
scene.text: In Jesus’ century, would-be deliverers drew crowds by promising wonders; Josephus tells of Theudas, who claimed he would part the Jordan (compare Acts 5:36). The leaders had already seen Jesus heal and cast out demons. They wanted a sign on their own terms.

scene.label: A good eye
scene.text: The Greek word for “good” here means single or sound: a healthy eye that lets the light in. In Jewish speech the eye also showed the heart. Proverbs blesses “a generous eye” (22:9) and warns of “an evil eye” that grasps after riches (28:22).

witnesses.matthew: Spells out the sign: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, a plain pointer to Jesus’ burial and resurrection. Matthew ends with “this wicked generation,” so the returning spirit becomes a warning to Israel itself, stirred by John’s and Jesus’ preaching but left empty.
witnesses.luke: Ties the demand for a sign to the Beelzebub debate and adds the woman who blessed Jesus’ mother; Jesus turns her blessing from family ties to obedience (compare Luke 8:21). Luke alone closes the scene with the lamp and the eye, so that the answer to people demanding a sign is a warning about their own sight.

seeing.reveals: Jesus claims to be greater than the prophet who brought Nineveh to repentance and greater than Israel’s wisest king. His death and resurrection would be the one sign that settles who He is.
seeing.living: A reformed life without Jesus is a swept house left empty, and it does not stay empty. Jesus does not call us to tidy up our lives on our own but to receive Him, and to hear the word of God and keep it. The sign-seekers had the Light standing in front of them; Jesus warned that the trouble lay in their own eye: “take heed that the light which is in you is not darkness.”
seeing.ponder: What sign are you still waiting for before you trust Jesus fully, when He has already given you the empty tomb?

preaching.big_idea: The risen Jesus is God’s final sign; nothing more will be given, and nothing more is needed.
outline: The sign of the buried and risen Son (39–40)
Witnesses who will rise in judgment (41–42)
The danger of an empty house (43–45)
preaching.watch_for: Matthew 12 shows Jesus greater than the temple (12:6), greater than Jonah and greater than Solomon (12:41–42). Each comparison lifts Him above the best that Israel had received from God.
